key_insight: Two deep neural networks enable fast inverse design of SRF cavity and transmon geometries from desired electromagnetic and qubit-cavity targets.
engineering_relevance: This reduces costly iterative simulation for superconducting quantum hardware design, accelerating the search for bosonic-quantum-computing device configurations.
method: DNN #1 maps target cavity observables to candidate 3D SRF cavity geometries.
DNN #2 maps target qubit-cavity parameters (g, νq, α) to transmon design and placement.
Candidates are validated with end-to-end re-simulation to check target matching.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovered designs matching targets within about 5% for cavities and about 2% for transmons after re-simulation.
watch_item: Inverse design is one-to-many, so multiple geometries may satisfy the same target and deployment still depends on high-fidelity simulation/validation.
paper_title: Neural-Network Inverse Design of SRF Cavities and Transmons for Bosonic Quantum Computation
